solution: There are C₁₂ = (1/13)·binom(24,12) = 208012 paths that stay on or above the diagonal. By the reflection principle, the numbers of valid path segments are: from the origin to (3,6), 48; from (3,6) to (12,12), 2002; from the origin to (8,10), 11934; from (8,10) to (12,12), 9; and from (3,6) to (8,10), 117. Inclusion–exclusion therefore gives 208012 − 48·2002 − 11934·9 + 48·117·9 = 55054.
insight: For a path of n steps starting at height h ≥ 0 above the diagonal, with u north steps, the number that never goes below the diagonal is binom(n,u) − binom(n,u+h+1).
insight_justification: There are binom(n,u) unrestricted paths. Reflecting each path through its first visit to height −1 gives a bijection from the invalid paths to paths starting at height −h−2 and ending at the same height. These reflected paths have u+h+1 north steps, so there are binom(n,u+h+1) of them.
